Hi Sarah — great to hear this is moving forward. Short answers up front: yes (automatic fallback) and yes (telemetry gating). I've attached a draft policy and a simple thresholds spreadsheet you can review.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Canary scope: 5% traffic, gradually ramp to 20% across 4 hours.
- Safety gates (automated): 3 consecutive 5-minute windows where error rate > 1% OR p99 latency > 900ms OR increase in token failure rate > 0.5% triggers an automatic pin to the previous stable model and traffic rollback.
- Pin behavior: immediate routing of new requests to stable model variant; existing in-flight tokens served but KV cache invalidated for canary variant to avoid contamination.
- Human oversight: Ops and customer success alerted, but no manual approval required to rollback.
- SLA carveout: we can offer a temporary, scoped waiver for the canary period (max 24h) provided the policy above is enforced and we have signed acceptance.

Next steps: Marcus can outline telemetry and the exact webhook/alert behavior; Laura can approve the limited SLA waiver language. If you agree I'll prepare a DocuSign for the waiver and book a 30-min runbook review.

Looping in the engineering details so everyone's aligned. Quick technical notes and constraints:

- Telemetry we can evaluate in near-real time: request error rate, model reject rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, sudden distributional shifts (via embedding drift heuristics).
- Automated trigger: we will implement a sliding window detector (5-minute windows, 1-minute sample cadence). A trigger requires meeting an absolute threshold AND a relative delta from baseline to avoid noisy rollbacks.
- Threshold recommendations (provisional): error rate > 1% AND >= 2x baseline for 3 windows; p99 latency > 900ms AND >= 30% increase vs baseline; token dropout delta > 0.5%.
- Pin semantics: we support immutable pinning of a variant ID. Once pinned, routing is immediate. We will also publish an audit log entry with reason and telemetry snapshots.
- Caveat: certain degradations (e.g., slow token decode due to cache warming) can look like high p99 early in rollout; that's why we require baseline-relative checks. We recommend a short warmup period (10 minutes) during the first ramp to stabilize caches.

I've attached the telemetry spreadsheet and a short runbook draft with play-by-play steps for automated rollback and manual remediation.

- Marcus

Sarah / team — brief yes from Product Ops with conditions. I'm approving a scoped SLA waiver for a single canary window with these required constraints:

1) Scoped region: us-west only for the canary.
2) Canary duration: max 4 hours per controlled rollout; total carveout can be up to 24 hours across multiple stagings but each segment needs an automated rollback policy attached.
3) Automated rollback: triggers on the telemetry rules Marcus listed. Rollback must be immediate and must record an immutable audit entry with telemetry snapshot.
4) Pin policy: pinned variant must be the last known stable variant ID — no partial traffic mixing after pin.
5) Post-incident review: if an automatic rollback occurs, Redwood will provide a telemetry bundle (p99 traces, 1% sampled requests, and error logs) to HedgeCo SREs within 4 business hours.
6) Acceptance: HedgeCo must sign the attached waiver (DocuSign link) acknowledging the temporary SLA carveout.

Assumptions: HedgeCo continues to receive standard monitoring and we reserve the right to refuse waive for production changes that impact regulated workflows without further security review.

I'll sign off on the DocuSign language once procurement confirms.
